newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes up on bullish Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes up on bullish Tokyo.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher again in tandem with the strong futures market in Tokyo but buying interest remained weak, traders said.
"There's still little consumer interest, but buyers are sitting up to watch the market because of Tokyo," said a dealer.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted market indicator price for November RSS1 buyer at 311.50 cents ($1.23) a kg, up two cents from Monday. November SMR 20 was also a cent higher at 309.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 306 cents, SMR 10 at 307, SMR 5 at 318, SMR L at 342, SMR CV at 362 and drum latex at 233.
"I haven't heard of any buying today but I think if the calling comes for SMR 20, it'll be around 304," said a dealer.
The Malaysian rubber market has been depressed for most of this month, with notable absence by Chinese, European and Middle East buyers who did active short-covering until August.
The INRO five-day average rose to 239.47 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 28 from 239.13 on Oct 25. The daily indicator was higher at 240.64 against 239.50.
